# `Q-3-55` — NoteDefinitionFencedBlock Not Supported in ANSI Format

> Fenced note definitions cannot be rendered in ANSI terminal
> output.

## What this means

A fenced note definition is the multi-paragraph form of a
footnote — the body lives inside a fenced block attached to the
note reference. The ANSI writer (used when rendering to a
terminal) does not render footnotes at all, regardless of form.

## Why this happens

Your document uses the fenced form of a note definition and you
rendered to ANSI output.

## How to fix

Render to a different format. HTML, PDF, and the markdown
writers all handle fenced footnotes. If the body is short
enough, you can also rewrite it as a one-line inline footnote
(`text^[body]`).

## Related

- `Q-3-54` — the same limitation for one-line `[^id]: body`
  definitions.
- `Q-3-11` — the same limitation for the qmd writer.
